mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, thereby producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 8% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 8% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO falls by more than 1% month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL over two months signals a restrictive monetary policy coinciding with falling inflation, which raises real interest rates and reduces equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS rises and CPIAUCSL falls for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase of at least 2% in real personal savings (RSAFS) combined with a decline in consumer spending (HOUST) indicates households are saving more and spending less, which reduces near-term demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > +2% and HOUST < 0% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS rises by more than 2% and HOUST falls for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS grows by more than 0.5% month-over-month for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent year-over-year increase of at least 4% in the housing starts index (HOUST) signals a recovery in residential construction demand, which boosts related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST rises by more than 4% year-over-year.
